_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-20 19:06:56Z)**_

Verified end-to-end. Here's what I found and what I'd recommend.

## Answers to your questions

**Is the file generated?** Yes — on first run, SpecStory writes **two** fully-commented template configs (both the same template, all lines commented out):

- `~/.specstory/cli/config.toml` — **user-level**, applies to every project
- `./.specstory/cli/config.toml` — **project-level**, overrides user-level (only for uncommented keys)

Both are already present here; the project-level one is even committed. `specstory check` shows both under "Configuration Files".

**Why the project file is the wrong lever for "newly built dev containers":** it lives in the bind-mounted workspace, so a rebuild never touches it — but it also only helps *this* repo. Any project that copies `.devcontainer/` gets the warning again until someone edits its own `.specstory/`.

**Why `sed` is the wrong tool:** at `docker build` time the file doesn't exist yet (SpecStory generates it on first *run*), so there's nothing to sed. You'd need a `postCreateCommand` hack, and it's brittle against template changes across versions.

## Recommendation: ship a user-level config at build time

Exactly the pattern the Dockerfile already uses for Codex (`.devcontainer/Dockerfile:140`):

```dockerfile
COPY --chown=${USERNAME}:${USERNAME} specstory-config.toml /home/${USERNAME}/.specstory/cli/config.toml
```

with a new `.devcontainer/specstory-config.toml` (SPDX header, hand-written, minimal). I tested this: a pre-seeded user config is **not overwritten** on first run, is reported as valid by `specstory check`, and with `[cloud_sync] enabled = false` the warning is gone on `specstory sync` in this repo. The committed project-level file (all-commented) doesn't override it.

Since `~/.specstory` isn't persisted across rebuilds, baking it into the image is also the *only* way it survives — which is precisely what you want.

## What I'd put in it

| Section | Setting | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `[cloud_sync]` | `enabled = false` | The warning you're seeing. Local-only is the documented mode in README. |
| `[analytics]` | `enabled = false` | This is the "telemetry" you mean: anonymous usage analytics, on by default. |
| `[version_check]` | `enabled = false` | **Suggested.** Version is pinned by `SPECSTORY_VERSION` and can't be upgraded in-container anyway, so the startup call to GitHub is pure noise (and a network call on every invocation). |

Notes on the rest of the template:

- `[telemetry]` is OTLP span export — **off unless `endpoint` is set**, so nothing to do. I'd leave it alone rather than add `prompts = false`, which is inert without an endpoint.
- `[redaction] enabled` — default `true`, **keep it**. It scrubs keys from saved markdown, which matters given `.specstory/history/` gets committed.
- `[local_sync] local_time_zone = true` — I'd **not** set it: existing history filenames use `…Z` UTC and the container is UTC anyway; mixing would break sort order.
- `[providers] codex_cmd` — not needed; `codex` resolves to the wrapper via `PATH` and the docs already say `specstory run codex` goes through it.
- `[logging]`, `[resume]` — leave defaults.

Also worth a README line under *SpecStory* saying cloud sync/analytics/version check are pre-disabled and where to override (project-level file or flags), plus a `decisions.md` entry.

=== README SpecStory section ===
## SpecStory

SpecStory wraps a terminal agent and auto-saves the conversation as markdown under
`.specstory/history/` in the project — your bind-mounted workspace, so transcripts land on
your host and survive the container.

```bash
specstory check          # which agents it can see
specstory run claude     # Claude Code, with auto-save
specstory run codex      # Codex, with auto-save
specstory watch          # save sessions from an agent you start yourself
specstory sync           # convert sessions that already happened in this directory
specstory search <query> # search past sessions
```

All of that is local-only and needs no account; `specstory login` and `specstory skills` are
the cloud (Pro) features.

**Before rebuilding the container, run `specstory sync`.** Agent state lives in the container's
home — `~/.claude`, `~/.codex` — and is not mounted, so it is lost on rebuild. `sync` writes
every Claude Code and Codex session for this directory to `.specstory/history/`, which is on
your host. To be able to *resume* a session afterwards rather than just read it, also copy the
raw transcripts out and back:

```bash
cp -a ~/.claude/projects .claude-backup/                 # before the rebuild (git-ignored)
cp -a .claude-backup/projects ~/.claude/ && claude --resume   # after
```

**Before committing `.specstory/history/`, read it.** Transcripts can contain keys, paths and
internal detail. Only `.specstory/debug/` is git-ignored by default.

## llama-server on the host

=== decisions.md (tail) ===
decisions.md
verifying-changes.md
stale and imply the container is Qwen-specific. The script's workflow is model-neutral; the
per-model patch table is the only model-specific part.

## 2026-09-20 — `model = "local"` kept although the server ignores it

Single-model llama-server ignores the `model` field. Kept as the fallback for when the wrapper
cannot reach the server at launch.

## 2026-09-20 — bwrap shim instead of `systempaths=unconfined` (temporary)

Codex's sandbox failed at `--proc /proc` (Docker's masked `/proc`; openai/codex#44329). The
Docker-side fix unmasks `/proc/kcore`, `/proc/sys` etc. for the whole container to serve one
tool, and the container's isolation is the outer moat. Landlock-only mode (`use_legacy_landlock`)
panics under `workspace-write` in 0.155.1. The shim reproduces Codex's own `--no-proc` fallback
at the PATH level; it lives in `/usr/local/bin` rather than `~/.local/bin` because Codex skips a
`bwrap` found under the current directory, which `~` can be. It is a stopgap: remove it once
openai/codex#44329 is fixed, not a permanent part of the container.

## Earlier (from git history)

- No root, no sudo, setuid stripped, `no-new-privileges`: the agent runs confined to `vscode`;
  root work is done via `docker exec -u root` from the host. (README → *Working as root*)
- Codex checksums pinned in the Dockerfile, not exposed as build args, so version and digest
  can't drift apart. (README → *Download verification*)
- Everything installed at build time; no `postCreateCommand`, so container creation is offline.

## Build performance

- BuildKit cache mounts hold apt's `.deb` downloads and package lists between builds.
- Layers are ordered coldest first: apt, then uv, then the pinned SpecStory and Codex downloads.
- `codex-config.toml`, `codex-wrapper.sh` and `bwrap-shim.sh` are copied after the toolchain, so editing them rebuilds only trivial layers.
- `seccomp.json` is a run-time option, not part of the image; changing it needs a container restart, not a rebuild.

# Verifying changes to the container configuration

There are no tests; every change has a concrete check. Show the output, don't assert.
The live-server and Codex probes are in `.devcontainer/agent_docs/codex-llama-server.md`.

| Changed | Check |
|---|---|
| Any `*.sh` | `shellcheck <file>`, then run it for real, against `$LLAMA_SERVER_URL` if it talks to the server |
| `seccomp.json` | `jq -e '.defaultAction and (.syscalls\|length) > 30'`; only a container recreate proves the rest |
| `devcontainer.json` `runArgs` | Needs a recreate. Cannot verify from inside — say so and give the user the in-container check |
| `devcontainer.json` `features` / `devcontainer-lock.json` | `npx --yes @devcontainers/cli@latest upgrade --workspace-folder . --dry-run` prints the lock the CLI would write; diff it against the committed file. This is the one CLI command that works without Docker (`read-configuration` and the rest shell out to `docker` first) |
| `Dockerfile` | Needs a rebuild. Cannot verify from inside — say so. A wrapper/config copied by hand into the running container (e.g. `~/.local/bin/codex`) is a stand-in until then; say that too |
| `bwrap-shim.sh` | Copy to `~/.local/bin/bwrap` as a stand-in (also first on PATH), then the two `codex sandbox` probes in the probes doc and a `codex exec -s workspace-write` that touches a file |
| `codex-config.toml` / `codex-wrapper.sh` | `codex exec -s read-only "Reply with the single word OK"`, then inspect the newest rollout (probes doc) |
| README command snippets | Run them exactly as written |
| `.devcontainer/AGENTS.md`, `.devcontainer/agent_docs/` | Must make sense in a project that is *not* this one: no paths or facts specific to this repo |

# SpecStory user-level config. Copied to ~/.specstory/cli/config.toml at build time, so it
# applies in every project opened in this container; SpecStory leaves it alone on first run.
# A project's own .specstory/cli/config.toml, or a CLI flag, overrides any key set here.
# Every other key keeps its default; the full template with all of them is the one SpecStory
# writes into a project on first run.

[cloud_sync]
# Local-only: no account, so no "Cloud sync not available" warning on every sync.
enabled = false

[analytics]
# Anonymous product-usage analytics.
enabled = false
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
import re,io
p='.devcontainer/Dockerfile'
s=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read()
old='''# Points Codex at the host's llama-server. Edit this file to change model or endpoint.
COPY --chown=${USERNAME}:${USERNAME} codex-config.toml /home/${USERNAME}/.codex/config.toml
'''
new=old+'''
# SpecStory defaults for every project (cloud sync and analytics off). Shipped at build time
# because ~/.specstory is not persisted; a project's .specstory/cli/config.toml overrides it.
COPY --chown=${USERNAME}:${USERNAME} specstory-config.toml /home/${USERNAME}/.specstory/cli/config.toml
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
open(p,'w',encoding='utf-8').write(s.replace(old,new))
PY
sed -n 138,148p .devcontainer/Dockerfile

```text
# Points Codex at the host's llama-server. Edit this file to change model or endpoint.
COPY --chown=${USERNAME}:${USERNAME} codex-config.toml /home/${USERNAME}/.codex/config.toml

# SpecStory defaults for every project (cloud sync and analytics off). Shipped at build time
# because ~/.specstory is not persisted; a project's .specstory/cli/config.toml overrides it.
COPY --chown=${USERNAME}:${USERNAME} specstory-config.toml /home/${USERNAME}/.specstory/cli/config.toml

# `codex` on PATH resolves to this wrapper (~/.local/bin precedes /usr/local/bin below),
# which passes llama-server's actual context size to the real binary at launch.
COPY --chown=${USERNAME}:${USERNAME} --chmod=0755 codex-wrapper.sh /home/${USERNAME}/.local/bin/codex
```

## Download verification

Every artifact fetched during the build is authenticated, and every version is pinned —
pinning is what makes a checksum meaningful in the first place.

| Artifact | How it is verified |
|---|---|
| apt packages | GPG signatures on the Debian repo metadata (apt does this itself) |
| uv / uvx | SHA256 from the release's `.tar.gz.sha256`, checked before install |
| SpecStory CLI | SHA256 from the release's `checksums.txt`, checked before install |
| Codex CLI | SHA256 pinned in the Dockerfile — upstream publishes none (see below) |
| Dev container features | Digests in `devcontainer-lock.json`, checked by the devcontainer CLI |
| Base image | Tag only — pin a digest to harden (see below) |
